effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per opcode in the Mantle specification's Opcodes table plus one for the unknown-code rule, in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in logos-blockchain-core that fails on 0.3.0 for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Logos Blockchain is a Rust workspace (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.lock committed). Package names carry a `logos-blockchain-` prefix the directory names lack; the `name` field of each crate's Cargo.toml is authoritative. The audited ref is the release tag 0.3.0 (commit 1da2d9d69a80452cf6b5d0e68304762d510c8a6c); record the resolved commit in the report. The specification in the prompt is one section of the Bedrock v1.1 Mantle specification LIP as published in the logos-lips repository at commit fddc2c1 (the 2026-10-08 Bedrock snapshot); each operation's payload, proof, gas, validation and execution are audited by the briefs for the Channel, SDP, Leader, Proof of Work and Transfer operation sections.

The Opcodes section is the table of operation codes: which numeric code names which operation, which proof type each operation carries, and which codes are reserved or unassigned. Its requirements are that table's rows and the rule for unknown codes.

Where the table lives in the code:
- core/src/mantle/ops/op.rs and ops/mod.rs (package `logos-blockchain-core`): the `Op` enum and its opcode mapping. ops/serde_.rs: how an opcode is read and written. ops/op_ref.rs, ops/op_proof.rs, ops/op_proof_ref.rs: the operation-to-proof pairing. core/src/mantle/transactions/codec.rs: the transaction codec that dispatches on the opcode, including what happens on an unknown code.
- Adjacent, outside the unit: the Mantle Transaction Encoding LIP (the byte layout of each operation, audited by another brief).

Running tests: the gate runs the unit's package with cargo-nextest, which is what CI uses (`.github/workflows/code-check.yml` runs the whole workspace that way; the whole workspace is too large for this container, so the gate is narrowed to the unit). `cargo nextest run --locked -p <package> --all-features` runs one package; `cargo test --locked -p <package> --all-features -- <filter>` works too. `.config/nextest.toml` marks a unit test slow after 30 s and kills it after 2 min. ZK proof dependencies come as prebuilt circuit crates (`lbc-*-sys` with the `prebuilt` feature) and the verifier links rapidsnark statically, so the first build compiles C++ and takes a while; nothing needs a running node, docker, or downloaded circuit files. New proof tests go in the owning crate's tests/ directory or as a `#[cfg(test)]` module file under src/ named by finding id. Treat code comments that cite a spec paragraph as claims to check.
